top_signals.title: Appointment of Chair and Deputy Chair of the Enforcement Decision Making Committee (EDMC)
top_signals.summary: Following an external recruitment process, the Bank of England (the Bank) has appointed Nicholas Segal as Chair of its Enforcement Decision Making Committee (EDMC), and Peter King as Deputy Chair, with effect from 1 August 2026.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Glacier collapse behind Nepal flood highlights region’s climate risk
top_signals.summary: Similar events are becoming more frequent as global warming accelerates the ongoing thaw in the Himalayas.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Mixed signals, research findings, and policy judgements − speech by Catherine L. Mann
top_signals.summary: Given at the Natixis CIB Private Debt Forum

top_signals.title: 15,000 operational days lost due to US submarine maintenance delays, GAO finds
top_signals.summary: Maintenance delays for U.S. submarines have "resulted in an estimated $3.4 billion in costs to sustain" crews and boats that were not operational.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Marines fielding new laser sights at School of Infantry
top_signals.summary: The Marine Corps introduced the Squad Aiming Laser to students at its North Carolina school.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Chainalysis says global crypto taxable activity topped $457 billion in 2025
top_signals.summary: Chainalysis estimates at least $457 billion in onchain taxable crypto activity in 2025, with CARF covering only 14%.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Digital asset volatility and institutional crypto positioning changes.

top_signals.title: White House bans foreign-made equipment for power generation over cyber backdoor concerns
top_signals.summary: The Trump administration is banning the acquisition of foreign-made components used to manage electricity and power, alleging that “certain foreign actors are increasingly creating and exploiting vulnerabilities” in the technology.
